You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A parent who has experienced their own challenges in adjusting to new environments and provides unconditional support
You are 43 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: some college. Your occupation: another field. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): weekly.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

Let me look at this board carefully. It's Black to move, and Black is behind 20-34. That's a big deficit, but the endgame can change things a lot.

Legal moves for Black: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8.

Let me think through each move and what it flips, then what White can do, etc. But I'm told not to simulate the full gameplay, and I have limited time. Let me look at the positions.

Move g2: Looking at row 2, W B W W B W . B. If I play g2, does it trap anything? To the left of g2 is f2=W, e2=B. So yes, g2 traps f2? Wait, e2 is B, so between g2 and e2: f2=W. So f2 flips. Any other lines? g2 row 2: f2=W, e2=B, so that's one flip. Diagonals/up/down? g1=W, doesn't help. g3=W, g4=W, etc down column g: g3=W, g4=W, g5=W, g6=W, g7=W, g8=W. No B below in that column. h2 is B, but that doesn't help since no Ws between g2 and h2. So g2 flips only f2.

After g2: f2 becomes B. Then White plays... but this seems minor.

Move b6: Row 6 is W . B W W B W B. b6 is between a6=W and c6=B. So yes, b6 flips nothing? Wait, between b6 and c6=B? No, c6 is already B, a6 is W but that's to the left. Actually, to flip, we need a line of opponent discs ending in our disc. From b6: left to a6=W, but no B beyond a6 (it's edge). Right to c6=B, but no Ws between because b6 is empty and c6 is adjacent B. Wait, b6 right: adjacent c6 is B, so no line. Left: adjacent a6 is W, then edge, no B. Down: b7=., b8=.. Up: b5=B, adjacent. Diagonal: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W — no B beyond? h7=B! So b6-diag to h7: c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 are all W — that's 5 discs. Does b6 to h7 work? Let me check: direction is down-right. b6 to c7, d8? Wait b6 to c7 is down-right. c7=W, d8=., so not reaching h7. Actually h7 is same row? No, h7 is row 7. Let me map: b6 -> c7 (down-right) -> d8 (down-right). d8 is W. Beyond d8 is e9 (off board). So no.

Direction down-left: a7=. So no.
Direction up-left: a5=B? a5 is B, but b6 to a5 is up-left and between is nothing (adjacent). So no flip.
Up-right: c5=W, d5=W, e5=B. So c5,d5 are between b6 and e5. Yes! b6 -> c5 -> d5 -> e5. c5 and d5 flip. 
Down: b7=., no.
Up: b5=B, adjacent, no W between.

Also from b6, up-left: a5=B... no W between.
Wait, b6 up-right we established c5=W, d5=W, e5=B. So 2 flips.
Any other? What about vertical up: b5=B adjacent. No.
So b6 flips c5 and d5.

That's good, gains 2 and possibly more.

Move a7: Let's see. a7 is empty. Column a: a1=., a2=W, a3=., a4=B, a5=B, a6=W, a7=., a8=.
If a7, up is... a6=W, a5=B. So a6 flips! Down: a8=., nothing. Right: b7=., c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. So b7 is empty, so next is c7=W — but need contiguous, and need to end at B. c7,d7,e7,f7,g7,h7: all W until h7=B? Wait c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. Yes! But is b7 skipped? From a7, moving right: b7=. The line has to be contiguous opponent discs with no gaps. Since b7 is empty, the line in direction right is broken immediately. Actually to the right: b7 is empty, so no line.

Diagonal up-right from a7: b6=., so no.
Diagonal down-right: b8=., no.
Diagonal up-left: off board.
So a7 only flips a6? Wait, also check row 7: a7 right... b7=., so no. What about down? a8=.. 

Wait, a7 is on the edge. Let me check all 8 directions carefully:
- Up (row decreases): a6=W, a5=B => a6 flips.
- Down: a8=. => none.
- Right: b7=. => none.
- Up-right: b6=. => none.
- Down-right: b8=. => none.
Left/up-left/down-left off board.

So a7 flips only a6. That's 1 disc, and then a7 becomes stable? Not necessarily.

Move b7: Row 7: . . W W W W W B. b7 is empty. 
- Left: a7=. no.
- Right: c7=W, d7=W, e7=W, f7=W, g7=W, h7=B. Yes! So c7-g7 flip. That's 5 discs!
- Up: b6=. no.
- Down: b8=. no.
- Up-right: c6=B, adjacent, not opponent first.
- Up-left: a6=W, beyond is edge, no B.
- Down-right: c8=., no.
- Down-left: a8=., no.
Also maybe up: b6=., b5=B — but b6 is empty, gap.

Wait also up direction: b6 is empty. But what about up-left diagonal? a6=W then edge. No. 
What about other directions? Let's check b7 and the B at e5? No, not in line. b7 to e4? Not a straight line.

Actually b7 down-left: a8=., no.
So b7 flips 5 Ws (c7,d7,e7,f7,g7). That's huge! And occupies b7.

Then what does White do? After b7, row 7 becomes B B B B B B B B (all B). That's a whole row! But White might have moves... Actually after b7, row 7 is all B. Then a7 is still empty, and White might have moves elsewhere. But this is very strong.

Move b8: Row 8: . . . W B W W B. b8 empty.
- Up: b7=. no.
- Right: c8=., no. 
Wait c8 is empty? Looking at board: c8=. yes. d8=W.
- Down: off.
- Left: a8=. no.
- Up-right: c7=W, d6=W, e5=B? Let's see: c7=W, d6=W, e5=B. So c7 and d6 flip! That's 2 discs.
- Up: b7=., b6=., b5=B? But gap at b7 and b6, so no line.
- Up-left: a7=. no.
- Right to c8 is empty, can't start there.

What about to e8? That's not in line. Up-right from b8: c7,d6,e5 — yes c7,d6 are Ws ending at B. So 2 flips. Also maybe right? c8=., then no. 

Move c8: 
- Up: c7=W, c6=B? Wait c7=W, c6=W? c6 is W? No, looking: row 6: W . B W W B W B. So c6=B. So from c8 up: c7=W, c6=B. So c7 flips. 
- Left: b8=., a8=.. no.
- Up-left: b7=., a6=W, but gap at b7 so no. Wait contiguous: b7 is empty, so direction up-left stops.
- Up-right: d7=W, e6=W, f5=B? Let's check: d7=W, e6=W (row 6 col e is W), f5... row 5 col f is W? Wait row 5: B B W W B W W B. f5 is W. g5 is W. h5 is B. So c8 up-right: d7=W, e6=W, f5=W, g5=W, h5=B. That's d7,e6,f5,g5 — 4 flips! 
- Left-up? Already checked.
- Right: d8=W, e8=B. So d8 flips! (1 flip). 

Wait c8 right: d8=W, e8=B, so d8 flips. Yes.
c8 up: c7=W, c6=B, so c7 flips. Yes.
c8 up-right: d7=W, e6=W, f5=W, g5=W, h5=B. That's 4 flips.
What about down? Off.
What about down-left? b7=., so no.
Down-right? d7? No down-right from c8 is d9 off.
Up-left? b7=. no.
Left? b8=., a8=.. no.

So c8 flips c7, d8, d7, e6, f5, g5 — total 6 discs. That's huge.

Wait, but b7 flips 5 discs and secures the entire row 7. c8 flips 6 discs but some might be flipped back. Let me double-check c8 up-right diagonal: from c8 to d7 (yes, W), e6 (row 6, col e — is it W? Row 6: W . B W W B W B. e6 is the 5th element? Let's map row 6: a6=W, b6=., c6=B, d6=W, e6=W, f6=B, g6=W, h6=B. Yes e6=W. Then f5: row 5 a5=B, b5=B, c5=W, d5=W, e5=B, f5=W, g5=W, h5=B. Yes f5=W. Then g5=W. Then h5=B. So yes, diagonal is c8-d7-e6-f5-g5-h5. Four Ws between c8 and h5.

And c8 up: c7=W, c6=B. Yes.
c8 right: d8=W, e8=B. Yes.

So c8 flips 1+1+4 = 6 Ws.

Now which move is best? Let's think about the resulting position and who has moves.

If b7: flips c7-g7. Row 7 becomes all B. But White's moves after b7: legal moves for White? After b7, board changes. Black gets +5 (5 W flipped +1 new = net +6? Actually he places 1, flips 5, so Black gains 6, White loses 5). Then it's White's turn.
After b7, row 7: B(B) at a7? No a7 still empty. b7=B, c7=B, d7=B, e7=B, f7=B, g7=B, h7=B. So row 7 becomes . B B B B B B B? Wait a7 is still empty. So White might be able to play a7? Let's see if a7 is legal for White. For White to play a7, it needs to trap Black. Adjacent: a8=., a6=B. So a6 is B, but left of a7 is edge, no. Right: b7=B adjacent. Up: a6=B, but need line of Black ending in White beyond? a5=B, a4=B. All Black, no White beyond. Down: a8=.. Diagonal: b8=.. So probably a7 would not be legal for White. Actually to trap, need White disc at end. There are no nearby White discs. So a7 is not legal for White.

What other empty squares after b7?
Empty before: a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b8, c8 (and b7 is now filled). 
After b7, still empty: a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b8, c8.
Can White play a1? Adjacent b1=W (already W). But needs trap Black. From a1, right: b1=W, no Black beyond in immediate? Actually b1 is W, so right from a1 goes to b1 which is same color, not opponent. Wait to trap Black, you need a line of Black ending in White. a1 right: b1=W — that's not Black. c1=W. So no.
Can White play h1? h2 is B. h1 left: g1=W. So left from h1: g1=W (not Black). f1=W. No.
Can White play g2? After b7, what about g2? g2 left: f2=W? No f2 was originally W but not flipped. g2 down: g3=W. g2 diag: h3=B, f3=W. So to trap Black from g2? We need White disc at end. h1 is empty, h2 is B, h3 is B. So direction to h3: g2-h3 is diagonal down-right. h3 is B. Beyond h3 is off board (i4). But you need your own color at end. So no.
What about White playing g2 to trap something else? Left: f2=W, e2=B. So between g2 and e2? f2 is W, not Black. So no.
Up: g1=W. No.
Down: g3=W. No.
So g2 probably not legal for White.

Can White play a3? a3 down-left etc. a4=B, b3=B. From a3, right: b3=B, c3=B. Need White at end. c3 is B. Going further: d3=W. So line b3-c3? Wait contiguous from a3: b3=B, c3=B, d3=W. Yes! So for White to play a3, it would flip b3 and c3 if there is a White at d3. d3 is W. So yes! a3 is legal for White. It flips b3 and c3 (Black to White).

Similarly b6: after b7, can White play b6? Let's see. From b6, down-right: c7=B. But now c7 is B (flipped by b7). b6 to d8 direction: c7=B, d8=W. Hmm, that's Black then White. Not unbroken opponent.
Other directions from b6: c5=B? Wait c5 was originally W but if b6 flips c5,d5, then after b7 they are still W because b7 didn't flip c5,d5. So if White plays later... but right now after b7 it's White's turn, not Black b6 yet. I was analyzing b7 as Black's move. So after Black plays b7, it's White's turn. White can play a3 as I said. Also White might be able to play b6? Let's check b6 for White. From b6: up-right c5=W (same), d5=W, e5=B. So even if b6 is White, no trap because ends on B. Wait for White to trap, need line of Black ending in White. From b6: c5 is W not Black. So no. Down-left a7=., no. a6=W. Up-left a5=B, but no White beyond (edge). So not legal.
b8 for White? b8 right c8=., down-right off. Up-right c7=B (now). So c7 is Black, d6=W, e7=W, f6=B... not contiguous of same color? Actually from b8 up-right: c7=B. That's not White to trap, need Black then White. c7 is Black, d6 is W, but they are not contiguous Black because only c7 is Black then d6 is White. So not a line of Black. b8 up: b7=B. Not legal.
c8 for White? c8 left b8=., up c7=B, up-left b7=B. So no.

So after b7, White might only have a3? And maybe something else. Let's check other empties.
h1: from h1, left g1=W, f1=W, e1=W, d1=W, c1=W, b1=W, a1=.. No Black contiguous ending with White because a1 is empty and beyond is edge.
a1: no.
g2: not legal as checked.
a7: right is b7=B. Not legal.
b6: seems not legal.
b8: not legal.
c8: not legal.
h1: not legal.
What about a3: yes, flips b3,c3.
Any others? What about White playing somewhere else... wait a1? Right: b1=W, not Black.
What about White playing g2? Maybe g2 could trap h3? g2-h3 is diagonal. h3=B. But need White beyond. i4 off board. No. Down: g3=W. Left: f2=W, e2=B. So from g2 left: f2=W (not Black). So no.

So after b7, White only move might be a3. Then Black moves again. Black might have many moves. If Black plays b7 and then White a3, then Black has... this is getting long.

What about c8? c8 flips 6 Ws: c7,d7,e7,f7,g7,d8,d7... wait g7 is one, d7 counted, e6, f5, g5. Let me recount: c8 right flips d8 (1). c8 up flips c7 (1). c8 up-right flips d7,e6,f5,g5 (4). Total 6. 

After c8, Black occupies c8, and flips those. Then White's turn. What legal moves for White? Empty squares after c8 fill c8. Empties: a1,h1,g2,a3,b6,a7,b7,b8.
White after c8:
- a1: right b1=W. No Black.
- h1: left g1=W. No Black.
- g2: let's recheck. Left f2=W, e2=B. So not line of Black. Right h2=B, no White beyond. Up g1=W. Down g3=W. Down-left f3=W. Down-right h3=B. So not legal.
- a3: right b3=B, c3=B, d3=W. Yes! flips b3,c3. Legal.
- b6: up-right c5=W? c5 is W. Not Black. Up b5=B, adjacent. Diagonal to e3? No. Right c6=B. So no.
- a7: up a6=W. Not Black. Right b7=.. No. Down a8=. Up-right b6=.. No.
- b7: up b6=.. Up-right c6=B. Not legal.
- b8: up-right c7=B (now). Not legal.
- Wait could White play a8? a8 is empty. From a8, right b8=. up a7=. up-right b7=. Not legal.
- What about White playing somewhere with Black line ending in White? Let's check a6? a6 is W already.

Actually after c8, maybe White has no moves except a3? Unless b7 allows something later. Let me check a7 for White after c8: a7 right b7=.. No.
Could White play b7? Need trap Black. b7 right c7=B now. Up-right c6=B. Not legal.
b8? up-right c7=B. Not legal.

So after c8, White also likely only has a3.

Now compare c8 vs b7. c8 gives +6 net flips immediately. b7 gives +5 net immediately. But c8 empties b7? No, b7 remains empty and might be useful later. b7 secures row 7 entirely, whereas c8 flips part of row 7 and other interior discs.

But which leaves Black with the most discs at the end? In Othello endgames, corners and edges matter. b7 is not a corner, but creates a solid block. However c8 flips more and also influences the bottom.

Wait, let's check if Black has another move after c8 before White gets a3? No, turns alternate. Black moves c8, then White moves a3 (forced maybe). Then Black moves again.

What if Black plays a3 later? 

Actually I need to think about the very end. With only a few moves, maybe we can simulate.

Let me try to trace after c8.

Current before c8: Black 20, White 34. Black plays c8. Discs flipped: c7,d7,e7,f7,g7,d8,d7,e6,f5,g5... wait d7 was flipped twice? No, from up-right: d7 is in up-right line? Let's be careful.

c8 up-right diagonal: squares are d7, e6, f5, g4? Wait g4 is W. h3 is B? Let's map coordinates properly.

c8 -> d7 (down-right? No, c8 is row 8 col c. Up-right would be row 7 col d? Row numbers increase downward. So from c8, "up" means decreasing row. But in standard board notation, row 1 is top. So from c8, up is c7. Up-right is b7? No, column increases to the right. So c8 up-right: row 7, col d. That's d7. Then row 6, col e: e6. Then row 5, col f: f5. Then row 4, col g: g4. Then row 3, col h: h3. 

Wait! I made a mistake! Up-right from c8 goes to d7, e6, f5, g4, h3. NOT g5! I misread the direction. Let me recheck.

c8 up-right:
- d7 (row 7, col d): W (row 7 is . . W W W W W B, so d7=W). Yes.
- e6 (row 6, col e): row 6 is W . B W W B W B. e6 is the 5th? a6=W, b6=., c6=B, d6=W, e6=W. Yes e6=W.
- f5 (row 5, col f): row 5 B B W W B W W B. f5 is W. Yes.
- g4 (row 4, col g): row 4 B B W B W W W B. g4 is W. Yes.
- h3 (row 3, col h): row 3 . B B W W W W B. h3 is B! Wait row 3 col h is B. So the line ends at h3 which is Black.

So the line c8 to h3 via d7,e6,f5,g4 flips d7, e6, f5, g4! Not g5! And h3 is Black, so yes, that line works. So 4 flips from that diagonal.

Also c8 right: d8 (row 8 col d) = W. e8 = B. So flips d8.
c8 up: c7 (row 7 col c) = W. c6 = B. So flips c7.

Total flips: d8 + c7 + d7 + e6 + f5 + g4. That's 6 discs. Correct.

So after c8, Black gains 7 (1 placed + 6 flipped), White loses 6. So Black 27, White 28. Almost even.

Now White to move after c8. Empty: a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, b8.
White legal moves? We need to recheck after c8.

White at a3: right a3->b3=B, c3=B, d3=W. So flips b3,c3. Legal yes.
Any other?
White at b6: Let's check thoroughly. From b6, up-left a5=B. Need White beyond. Beyond a5 is edge. No.
Up: b5=B. Need White beyond. b4=W! But is there a contiguous line of Black between? b6 to b4: between is b5=B. So yes? Wait direction up from b6 goes to b5=B (adjacent), then b4=W. So line is b5 (Black) ending in b4 (White). Does that work for White playing b6? If White plays at b6, b5 is Black. Then beyond b5 is b4=W (White). So yes! b6 would flip b5. That's one flip. Are there other lines? Left: a6=W. Need Black then White? a6 is White same color. So not opponent. Right: c6=B, beyond c6 is d6=W. So c6 is Black between b6 and d6? b6 (White newly placed) to c6=B to d6=W (White). Yes! That traps c6. So b6 flips c6 as well. Wait, d6 is W. So White plays b6, right direction: c6 is Black, d6 is White. So flips c6. Up direction: b5 is Black, b4 is White. Flips b5. Any other? Down: b7=.. Down-right: c7=B (now c7 was flipped to Black by c8). d8=W. So b6 to c7 (B) to d8 (W). That traps c7? No, c7 is Black now? Wait after c8, c7 was flipped to Black. So from b6 down-right: c7=B, d8=W. So that flips c7. That's another one. Down-left: a7=. No. Up-right: c5=W. Not Black. So White playing b6 after c8 flips b5, c6, c7! That's 3 flips. So b6 is legal for White.

White at a7: right b7=.. So no. Other directions?
White at b7: right c7=B. Beyond c7? d7 was flipped to Black. e7? e7 was flipped? Wait e7 was in the up-right from c8: c8 up-right included e6 and f5 and g4, but c7 and d7 were flipped? Let's see: c8 up flips c7. c8 right flips d8. c8 up-right flips d7,e6,f5,g4. So yes d7 is flipped to Black. e7 is still W? Wait row 7 after c8: a7=., b7=., c7=B, d7=B, e7=W? But wait c8 flips d7 (to B). e7 stays W. f7 stays W. g7 stays W. h7=B.

The key feature to check is **mobility and corners**: after c8, what strong replies does White get, especially around the empty corners **a1/a8/h1**? I’d compare c8 against the quieter legal moves by asking: “Which move leaves White with the fewest good replies?”

- b7: White has a3 and a devastating b6 (as I found earlier with b2-b5 flip). So b7 is bad.
- b6: White gets c8 (6 flips) and others. Bad.
- b8: White might get c8 or b7 etc.
- a7: flips only a6, small. Leaves White many options.
- g2: flips f2. Leaves c8 open for White. Bad.

Maybe c8 is still the best among them because at least after c8, Black gets the massive a3 if White plays b6. And c8 prevents White from the 6-flip c8. 

But what if the assistant is hinting that a quieter move is better? In endgames, sometimes "quieter" moves (those that don't give opponent many discs to flip) are better. But here White is ahead 34-20, so Black needs to flip many. The only way to do that is aggressive moves that create big swings.

Let me think about another candidate: a7. Black a7 flips a6. But then row a: a7=B, a6=B? Actually a6 becomes B. a5=B, a4=B. So Black secures the a-file from a4 to a7. But White can still play a8? parts.content:
Simple shortcut: **don’t count flips first; count White’s replies.** A quiet move is usually better if it leaves White with few/no moves, avoids giving a corner, or lets you take the last move in a region.

parts.content:
Yes — **parity** is basically the value of making the **last move in a region** when the board is nearly full.  

The deciding feature is **odd/even empty squares**: if an isolated area has an odd number of empties, the player who moves there first may also get the last move; if it has an even number, the second player often gets the last move. Last move matters because there’s no time for the opponent to flip those discs back, so a “quiet” parity move can beat a big flashy flip.
